title: burst-credit accounting leak in reserved pools causing transient tenant throttles
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Summary:
A handful of Dedicated customers observed unexpected 429 throttles during short burst windows yesterday (2025-01-27 22:00 - 22:40 UTC) despite showing available burst credits in the console. Initial alerts flagged sudden request rejections from the autoscaler layer for tenants using reserved pools with burst enabled.

Root cause hypothesis (so far):
- The burst credit accounting path in the reserved-pool allocator did not correctly reconcile credits after partial request retries that crossed an internal request-id boundary.
- When a request was retried by our serving runtime (for transient kernel OOM or scheduling preemption), the allocator subtracted burst tokens twice for what should have been a single logical request, draining the tenant's apparent burst headroom.
- The reconciliation job that runs hourly only fixes long-term drifts; the immediate effect was that the tenant hit a hard per-tenant throttle and started receiving 429s until either burst credits replenished or an operator ran a manual reconcile.

Why this is unique from past issues:
- Not a pool capacity shortage or autoscaler failure — cluster GPU headroom was available. This is an accounting leak localized to tenant-level burst credits across the request retry path.
- Previous incidents (ENG-27109, ENG-33112) focused on oversubscription and delayed scaling; this is a logic-level double-debit during retry/redirect flows.

Impact and scope:
- Affected 6 tenants across two reserved pools (ap-southeast-1 and eu-west-1) intermittently for ~40 minutes. One customer filed an urgent PD ticket (Account: BrightPatch) reporting user-facing timeouts and downstream errors.
- Console showed incorrect burst balances (positive) — misleading to both customers and on-call engineers.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Rolled back an internal retry optimization deployed 2025-01-26 that changed request-id assignment timing (hotfix rollout 2025-01-27 23:15 UTC). This restored single-debit behavior for new requests.
- Executed manual reconcile for the two impacted pools, restoring burst credit counters for affected tenants (2025-01-28 01:10 UTC).
- Notified impacted customers with an incident summary and ETA for a permanent fix.

Longer-term fix plan (this ticket):
- Fix double-debit bug in reserved-pool allocator when request retried after router-level redirect (patch + unit tests).
- Add idempotency guard keyed by canonical client request id across allocator path to prevent duplicate token consumption.
- Enhance observability: emit delta metrics when burst tokens are consumed and when a reconcile repairs a mismatch. Add an alert on token-consumption anomalies (sudden negative reconcile deltas > 1k tokens/min).
- Backfill reconciliation frequency and introduce a fast-check job (1m sampling) for tenant-level token drift during heavy bursts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Patch merged and deployed to staging with unit + integration tests proving single-token debit under retry scenarios.
- Canary rollout to one non-production reserved pool shows no double-debits under synthetic retry storm (load harness). Metrics delta within expected thresholds.
- New alerting firing thresholds validated in monitoring runbooks.
- Customer communications sent and follow-ups scheduled with impacted tenants.

Rollback plan:
- If new allocator guard causes request latency regressions > 10ms p95 or introduces deadlocks, revert to previous allocator and reapply a safer idempotency shim with backoff.

PR/Artifacts:
- Design note: drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/burst-accounting-design (internal)
- Staging test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-load-tests/pulls/210
- Hotfix rollback PR reference: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/1987

Notes on communication and follow-up items (postmortem threads):
- Engineering should coordinate with Console/Console Metrics team to ensure customers do not see inconsistent balances during reconciles.
- Product should evaluate a UX cue that indicates 'last reconcile at' so customers understand eventual-consistency window.
- Runbook update: add a step to force-reconcile tenant balances and to escalate to SRE if multiple tenants show mismatch in >2 pools.
